title: How a satellite takes a picture of Pokuase

scenes.caption: A satellite circles high above Ghana, about 786 km up.
Sunlight hits the ground and bounces back. The satellite's instrument measures that light.
The picture is made of tiny squares called pixels. In the red, green and blue bands each pixel is 10 metres wide on the ground.
Clouds block the view, so many pictures from one year are blended into one clear picture.
Put two years side by side to see what changed.
